evidence.reference_title: Absence of CFAP69 Causes Male Infertility due to Multiple Morphological Abnormalities of the Flagella in Human and Mouse.
evidence.snippet: Ultrastructural analysis of testicular sperm from the knockout mice showed severe disruption of flagellum structure, but histological analysis of testes from these mice revealed the presence of all stages of the seminiferous epithelium, indicating that the overall progression of spermatogenesis is preserved and that the sperm defects likely arise during spermiogenesis.

nodes.description: ICSI bypasses the motility defect. nodes.description: Biallelic stop-gain, frameshift and splice-site variants abolish or sharply reduce CFAP69 in the sperm flagellum. CFAP69 is concentrated in the midpiece of control sperm. Its precise structural role in mammalian sperm is not established: it carries predicted Armadillo-type repeats, and its Chlamydomonas orthologue is associated with the C1b projection of the central apparatus, so it is treated here as a structural component of the axoneme.
